Peeling off an isotropic part J=τ​I+KJ=\tau I+K with τ=13​tr​(J)\tau=\tfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{tr}(J) (so τ​I\tau I takes the orthogonal certificate with Q=IQ=I) and bounding the remainder KK by the operator or nuclear certificate, or peeling off the nearest orthogonal part J=λ​Q+KpolJ=\lambda Q+K_{\text{pol}} with Q=U​V⊤Q=UV^{\top} from the SVD and λ=13​tr​(Q⊤​J)\lambda=\tfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{tr}(Q^{\top}J), gives six certificates whose minimum is used for each edge,

αfull​(J)=min⁡{φ2​‖J‖op,12​‖J‖∗,34​|τ|+φ2​‖K‖op,34​|τ|+12​‖K‖∗,34​|λ|+φ2​‖Kpol‖op,34​|λ|+12​‖Kpol‖∗}\alpha_{\text{full}}(J)=\min\Bigl\{\tfrac{\varphi}{2}\|J\|_{\text{op}},\;\tfrac{1}{2}\|J\|_{*},\;\tfrac{3}{4}|\tau|+\tfrac{\varphi}{2}\|K\|_{\text{op}},\;\tfrac{3}{4}|\tau|+\tfrac{1}{2}\|K\|_{*},\;\tfrac{3}{4}|\lambda|+\tfrac{\varphi}{2}\|K_{\text{pol}}\|_{\text{op}},\;\tfrac{3}{4}|\lambda|+\tfrac{1}{2}\|K_{\text{pol}}\|_{*}\Bigr\} (A.7)
Theorem A.3 (Tight per-edge threshold).

With αfull\alpha_{\text{full}} from (A.7), the threshold

μ⋆​(J,h)=(1+ϵ)​maxi∈[N]​[∑k≠iαfull​(Ji​k)+23​bi]\mu_{\star}(J,h)\;=\;(1+\epsilon)\,\max_{i\in[N]}\Bigl[\,\sum_{k\neq i}\alpha_{\text{full}}(J_{ik})+\tfrac{2}{3}\,b_{i}\,\Bigr] (A.8)

obeys μ⋆≤λmin\mu_{\star}\leq\lambda_{\min} and the conclusion of Theorem A.1: for every λ≥μ⋆\lambda\geq\mu_{\star} and per-site-odd ψ\psi, ⟨ψ|H⁡(λ)|ψ⟩≥E0​‖ψ‖2\langle\psi|H(\lambda)|\psi\rangle\geq E_{0}\,\|\psi\|^{2}.

The proof is given in Appendix B.5.

On the canonical couplings the minimum lands on the physically right primitive. Heisenberg J=J0​IJ=J_{0}I gives αfull=34​|J0|\alpha_{\text{full}}=\tfrac{3}{4}|J_{0}| from the isotropic entry, recovering the textbook μ⋆=34​wdi\mu_{\star}=\tfrac{3}{4}\mathrm{wd}_{i}, that is 1.51.5 on the 1D unit chain rather than the universal φ≈1.618\varphi\approx 1.618; pure Ising or XY (JJ rank one) drops to 12​|J|\tfrac{1}{2}|J| through the nuclear entry; pure Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya stays at φ2​|D|\tfrac{\varphi}{2}|D|, the operator entry, since its singular values are dense.

Appendix B Proofs from Supp. Mat. S1

The five results stated in SM § S1 and Appendix A are proved here: Proposition S1.1, Theorem S1.2, Theorems A.1 and A.3, and Lemma A.2. Proposition S1.1 is elementary and can be checked by hand.

B.1 Proof of Proposition S1.1

Proof.

By the Peter–Weyl expansion above, ψ=∑𝑱,𝒎,𝒏c𝑱,𝒎,𝒏​Φ𝑱,𝒎,𝒏\psi=\sum_{\boldsymbol{J},\boldsymbol{m},\boldsymbol{n}}c_{\boldsymbol{J},\boldsymbol{m},\boldsymbol{n}}\,\Phi_{\boldsymbol{J},\boldsymbol{m},\boldsymbol{n}}, with −Δk-\Delta_{k} diagonal of eigenvalue jk​(jk+1)j_{k}(j_{k}+1) by (S1.26). B.2 Proof of Theorem S1.2

Proof.

Schur orthogonality gives, on one copy of GG,

∫GDm​n1/2​(q)¯​Dm′​n′1/2​(q)​𝑑q=12​δm​m′​δn​n′.\int_{G}\overline{D^{1/2}_{mn}(q)}D^{1/2}_{m^{\prime}n^{\prime}}(q)\,\mathrm{d}q=\frac{1}{2}\delta_{mm^{\prime}}\delta_{nn^{\prime}}. (B.2)

Peter–Weyl identifies the spin-12\tfrac{1}{2} sector with 𝒦N⊗ℋN\mathcal{K}_{N}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{N}, which is exactly ℱlin\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{lin}}. Since

dimιχ​(ℋN)=2Nanddimℱlin=4N,\dim\iota_{\chi}(\mathcal{H}_{N})=2^{N}\quad\text{and}\quad\dim\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{lin}}=4^{N}, (B.3)

the first inclusion in Eq. (S1.32) is strict for N≥1N\geq 1.

The central element −I∈G-I\in G acts on VjV_{j} as (−1)2​j​I(-1)^{2j}I. with the product over i≥2i\geq 2 omitted when N=1N=1.

Finally, on a per-site-odd Peter–Weyl block labelled by 𝒋=(j1,…,jN)\boldsymbol{j}=(j_{1},\ldots,j_{N}),

    =λmin​(J,h)1+ϵ​Q​(s)≤λmin​(J,h)​Q​(s).\displaystyle\;=\;\frac{\lambda_{\min}(J,h)}{1+\epsilon}\,Q(s)\;\leq\;\lambda_{\min}(J,h)\,Q(s).

    Assemble. Decompose any per-site-odd ψ=∑sψs\psi=\sum_{s}\psi_{s} over the orthogonal sectors. Using block-diagonality (1) on H^\hat{H} and the scalar action of C^\hat{C} from (1),

    ⟨ψ|H⁡(λ)|ψ⟩\displaystyle\langle\psi|H(\lambda)|\psi\rangle =∑s[⟨ψs|H^|ψs⟩+λ​Q​(s)​‖ψs‖2]\displaystyle\;=\;\sum_{s}\Bigl[\,\langle\psi_{s}|\hat{H}|\psi_{s}\rangle+\lambda\,Q(s)\,\|\psi_{s}\|^{2}\,\Bigr] (block-diagonal in ss)
    ≥∑s[E0​(ℋs)+λ​Q​(s)]​‖ψs‖2\displaystyle\;\geq\;\sum_{s}\Bigl[\,E_{0}(\mathcal{H}_{s})+\lambda\,Q(s)\,\Bigr]\,\|\psi_{s}\|^{2} (within-sector variational principle)
    ≥∑s[E0−B⁡(s)+λ​Q​(s)]​‖ψs‖2\displaystyle\;\geq\;\sum_{s}\Bigl[\,E_{0}-B(s)+\lambda\,Q(s)\,\Bigr]\,\|\psi_{s}\|^{2} (step 2: E0​(ℋs)≥E0−B⁡(s)E_{0}(\mathcal{H}_{s})\geq E_{0}-B(s))
    ≥∑sE0​‖ψs‖2\displaystyle\;\geq\;\sum_{s}E_{0}\,\|\psi_{s}\|^{2} (step 5 with λ≥λmin\lambda\geq\lambda_{\min})
    =E0​‖ψ‖2.\displaystyle\;=\;E_{0}\,\|\psi\|^{2}.

    For the all-12\tfrac{1}{2} sector s=(12,…,12)s=(\tfrac{1}{2},\dots,\tfrac{1}{2}) the raised set is empty, B⁡(s)=0B(s)=0 and Q⁡(s)=0Q(s)=0, and the chain collapses to the physical variational bound ⟨ψ12|H^|ψ12⟩≥E0​‖ψ12‖2\langle\psi_{\tfrac{1}{2}}|\hat{H}|\psi_{\tfrac{1}{2}}\rangle\geq E_{0}\,\|\psi_{\tfrac{1}{2}}\|^{2}.

∎

B.4 Proof of Lemma A.2 (per-edge certificates)

Proof.

Operator. Step (3b) of Appendix B.3 gives ‖S→i⊤​J​S→k‖(si,sj)≤‖J‖op​r​(si)​r​(sj)\|\vec{S}_{i}^{\top}J\vec{S}_{k}\|_{(s_{i},s_{j})}\leq\|J\|_{\text{op}}\,r(s_{i})r(s_{j}), and ≤‖J‖op​34\leq\|J\|_{\text{op}}\,\tfrac{3}{4} on (12,12)(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}), so the left side of (A.6) is at most ‖J‖op​[r⁡(si)​r​(sj)+34]\|J\|_{\text{op}}[r(s_{i})r(s_{j})+\tfrac{3}{4}]. The ratio [r⁡(si)​r​(sj)+34]/[q⁡(si)+q⁡(sj)][r(s_{i})r(s_{j})+\tfrac{3}{4}]/[q(s_{i})+q(s_{j})] over non-trivial pairs is largest at (32,12)(\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}), where it equals (152​32+34)/3=(5+1)/4=φ2(\tfrac{\sqrt{15}}{2}\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\tfrac{3}{4})/3=(\sqrt{5}+1)/4=\tfrac{\varphi}{2}.

Nuclear. For rank one J=σ​u​v⊤J=\sigma\,uv^{\top}, S→i⊤​J​S→k=σ⁡(u⋅S→i)​(v⋅S→k)\vec{S}_{i}^{\top}J\vec{S}_{k}=\sigma\,(u\!\cdot\!\vec{S}_{i})(v\!\cdot\!\vec{S}_{k}); each factor has operator norm ss (eigenvalues −s,…,s-s,\dots,s), so the pair norm is ≤|σ|​si​sj\leq|\sigma|\,s_{i}s_{j}, while on (12,12)(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}) the two ±12\pm\tfrac{1}{2} factors give |σ|/4|\sigma|/4. Then [si​sj+14]/[q⁡(si)+q⁡(sj)]≤12[s_{i}s_{j}+\tfrac{1}{4}]/[q(s_{i})+q(s_{j})]\leq\tfrac{1}{2}, because q⁡(si)+q⁡(sj)−2​(si​sj+14)=(si−sj)2+(si+sj)−2≥0q(s_{i})+q(s_{j})-2(s_{i}s_{j}+\tfrac{1}{4})=(s_{i}-s_{j})^{2}+(s_{i}+s_{j})-2\geq 0 for every non-trivial half-integer pair (si+sj≥2s_{i}+s_{j}\geq 2). Summing the rank-one pieces of the SVD gives 12​‖J‖∗\tfrac{1}{2}\|J\|_{*}.

Orthogonal. For J=λ​QJ=\lambda Q, Q∈𝒪⁡(3)Q\in\mathcal{O}(3), the rotated operators S~k=Q​S→k\tilde{S}_{k}=Q\vec{S}_{k} keep the Casimir ∑a(S~ka)2=sk​(sk+1)\sum_{a}(\tilde{S}_{k}^{a})^{2}=s_{k}(s_{k}+1), so S→i⋅S~k\vec{S}_{i}\!\cdot\!\tilde{S}_{k} is unitarily (detQ=+1\det Q=+1) or anti-unitarily (detQ=−1\det Q=-1) equivalent to S→i⋅S→k\vec{S}_{i}\!\cdot\!\vec{S}_{k}, whose pair operator norm is si​sj+min⁡(si,sj)s_{i}s_{j}+\min(s_{i},s_{j}) (the extreme total-spin multiplets). The ratio [si​sj+min+34]/[q⁡(si)+q⁡(sj)][s_{i}s_{j}+\min+\tfrac{3}{4}]/[q(s_{i})+q(s_{j})] peaks at (32,32)(\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{3}{2}), value (94+32+34)/6=34(\tfrac{9}{4}+\tfrac{3}{2}+\tfrac{3}{4})/6=\tfrac{3}{4}.

Additivity is the triangle inequality applied to each operator-norm term in (A.6). ∎

B.5 Proof of Theorem A.3 (tight per-edge threshold)

Proof.

By Lemma A.2 and its additivity each entry of (A.7) is a certificate (the isotropic and polar entries split JJ and sum a primitive on each part), and the minimum of certificates is a certificate, so αfull​(Ji​k)\alpha_{\text{full}}(J_{ik}) satisfies (A.6). Assigning it to the endpoints (a boundary edge has q⁡(12)=0q(\tfrac{1}{2})=0, so its whole weight lands on the raised site) and keeping the field bound j+12≤23​q​(j)j+\tfrac{1}{2}\leq\tfrac{2}{3}q(j) of Appendix B.3 (its step 5), steps (2) and (6) there go through with ∑kαfull​(Ji​k)\sum_{k}\alpha_{\text{full}}(J_{ik}) in place of φ2​wdi\tfrac{\varphi}{2}\mathrm{wd}_{i}. Since every entry of the minimum is ≤φ2​‖Ji​k‖op\leq\tfrac{\varphi}{2}\|J_{ik}\|_{\text{op}}, we have μ⋆≤λmin\mu_{\star}\leq\lambda_{\min}. ∎

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
